questions.q: A chemical-test report used for the section 24 license procedure must indicate that the person's blood-alcohol percentage was not less than .08, or that the person was under 21 and the percentage was not less than
questions.explanation: Section 24 requires the report to show a percentage not less than .08, or, if the person was under 21 at the arrest, a percentage not less than .02. The report must also show that the test was given by a trained and certified operator.

questions.q: A second violation of the junior-operator passenger restriction suspends the license for 180 days, and reinstatement also requires
options: Only payment of the reinstatement fee
A registrar-selected attitudinal program for young drivers
A new learner's permit held for one year
A parent's affidavit that the violation was necessary
questions.explanation: Section 8 says a junior operator suspended for a second or subsequent violation of that paragraph is not eligible for reinstatement until also completing the program the registrar selects. Completion of a program selected by the registrar that encourages attitudinal changes in young drivers.

questions.q: If the learner's-permit holder is under 18, the permit does not allow operation between midnight and 5 a.m. unless the accompanier is
questions.explanation: Section 8B states that midnight-to-5 a.m. limit and those two accompanier classes. The accompanier occupies the seat beside the driver. A parent or legal guardian with a valid license and at least one year of experience, or, for an emancipated minor, a person 21 or older with a valid license and at least one year of experience, in the seat beside the driver.

questions.q: A junior operator's license may be issued to a minor under 18 who has held a learner's permit at least six months and has
questions.explanation: Section 8(b) requires age 16 and one-half. Paragraph (a) requires the permit to have been held at least six months immediately before the application, with a driving record free of surchargeable incidents and without the alcohol, drug, and permit-suspension events the paragraph lists.

questions.q: How many hours of supervised driving must a teen in Massachusetts complete before getting a provisional license?
questions.explanation: Massachusetts requires 40 hours of supervised driving before the provisional license.

questions.q: In Massachusetts, what is the youngest age for a full, unrestricted car license?
questions.explanation: Massachusetts drivers can hold an unrestricted license at 18 years.

questions.q: How many questions are on the Massachusetts car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: The Massachusetts car knowledge test has 25 questions.

questions.q: What score do you need to pass the Massachusetts car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: You need 72% to pass the Massachusetts car knowledge test.

questions.q: In Massachusetts, a driver 21 or older is legally impaired at what blood alcohol concentration?
questions.explanation: In Massachusetts, drivers 21 and older are over the limit at 0.08% or more.

questions.q: In Massachusetts, a driver under 21 breaks the law at what blood alcohol concentration?
questions.explanation: Massachusetts sets the under-21 limit at 0.02%.

questions.q: In Massachusetts, how long is the license suspension for an adult's first refusal of a breath or blood test?
questions.explanation: A first refusal in Massachusetts brings a suspension of 180 days.

questions.q: Unless a sign says otherwise, what is the speed limit in a Massachusetts residential district?
questions.explanation: Massachusetts sets 30 mph in residential districts unless another limit is posted.

provenance.manual: Speed limit and advisory speed signs | Mass.gov

questions.q: What is the highest standard speed limit for cars on rural interstates in Massachusetts?
questions.explanation: Rural interstates in Massachusetts can be posted up to 65 mph for cars.

questions.q: When is a left turn on a red light allowed in Massachusetts?
options: From a one-way or two-way street onto a one-way street
Only from a one-way street onto a one-way street
questions.explanation: In Massachusetts, a left turn on red (after a full stop, where not prohibited) is allowed: only from a one-way street onto a one-way street.

questions.q: How is Massachusetts's seat belt law for adults enforced?
options: No seat belt law for adults
Primary: police can stop you just for not wearing a seat belt
Secondary: police can cite you only after stopping you for something else
questions.explanation: Massachusetts seat belt enforcement is secondary.

questions.q: Until what age must a child ride in a car seat or booster seat in Massachusetts?
questions.explanation: Massachusetts requires a car seat or booster until 8 years, with height or weight exceptions.
